findings.summary: AbiWord is a free, open-source word processor written in C++ and based on GTK+ since version 3. Originally developed by SourceGear Corporation and later adopted by the open-source community, it runs cross-platform including Linux, Windows, and macOS (via XQuartz). The application supports standard word processing features such as lists, indents, styles, tables, footnotes, and templates, as well as a Presentation view for screen-sized displays. It offers import/export filters for formats including .doc, .docx, .odt, and .rtf, with a native XML .abw format designed to reduce vendor lock-in. Collaboration is facilitated through GOCollab, supporting TCP and XMPP protocols. A US English-only grammar checker uses the Link Grammar parser. The interface mimics classic Microsoft Word for ease of migration, though direct cloning is no longer a priority.

mechanisms.title: Grammar checking via Link Grammar
mechanisms.explanation: AbiWord includes a US English-only grammar checking plugin that uses the Link Grammar parser, an open-source syntax theory and parser now developed by the AbiWord project. This was the first integrated grammar checker in a free word processor.

mechanisms.title: Cross-platform GTK+ rendering
mechanisms.explanation: Since version 3, AbiWord is based on GTK+ 3, enabling it to run cross-platform on Linux, Windows, and other systems. The macOS port has remained on version 2.4 since 2005 but can run non-natively through XQuartz.
